Subject: SIG follow-up: incident response notification windows and POC

Hi Camila,

Thanks for starting the SIG questionnaire. Two quick follow-ups from our Security team around incident response:

1) What is your standard time-to-customer-notification after you confirm a data-exfiltration incident? We need the baseline and any faster commitments for critical incidents.
2) Who are the operational POCs we should call for incident escalation (phone + backup)? Please include role, email, and mobile.
3) Can you provide an evidentiary artifact for your IR plan (playbook or SOC2 section) we can attach to the questionnaire?

We'd like to close this section by EOD Friday if possible. I'm copying our auditor (Claire) who will ingest any artifacts.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Luke
Luke Harris

lharris@greenfintech.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: incident response notification windows and POC

Hi Luke — thanks for the questions. Below are our IR-related responses you can paste into the SIG: 

1) Notification windows (high level):
- Initial customer notification: within 72 hours of confirmed data-exfiltration affecting customer data.
- For incidents classified Sev-1 (confirmed large-scale exposure or regulatory material impact), we target an initial notification within 24 hours and a follow-up update within 72 hours.
- We escalate to legal/compliance and engineering immediate on detection; times above are for customer-facing notifications after confirmation.

2) Operational POCs (primary + backup):
- Primary: Grace O'Connor, Head of Security Operations — grace.oconnor@redwood.com, +1 415-555-0199
- Backup: Dev Patel, Senior Solutions Engineer — dev.patel@redwood.com, +1 415-555-0207
- Legal escalation: Marcus Lin, Counsel — marcus.lin@redwood.com, +1 415-555-0177

3) Evidence we can share:
- Excerpt of our incident response playbook (redacted operational runbook): incident_response_playbook.pdf [Attachment].
- Latest SOC2 Type II attestation covering security controls: SOC2-2025-Attestation.pdf [Attachment].

4) EU/regulatory notes:
- For EU data subject incidents, Redwood will provide notification support and coordinate with customer counsel; any regulatory filing obligations remain the customer's responsibility unless explicitly agreed in the contract. We can sign an MSA addendum for joint-notice workflows if needed.

If you want these in a short Q&A paste for the SIG, I can format and add timestamps/more precise definitions of "confirmed" vs "suspected."

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
[Attachment: incident_response_playbook.pdf (13 KB)]

Grace — very helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups:

- Can you confirm whether the 24-hour initial notification for Sev-1 is a contractual commitment you're willing to take (MSA addendum), or an internal target? Our regulator wants to see contractual commitments for certain classes of incidents.
- For EU data subject incidents, we'd like Redwood to support regulatory filings (eg. liaise with local DPA) under an explicit process. Can Marcus propose language for an addendum?
- Claire (auditor) — can you confirm if the SOC2 artifact is sufficient for your intake, or do you need more (evidence of playbook tests / tabletop exercise logs)?

If we can get proposed addendum language and a redline by Friday, we'll progress the procurement queue.

Thanks,
Luke

Luke — quick legal note on behalf of Redwood: 

- We can commit to an initial customer notification within 24 hours for contractual "Sev-1" incidents where Redwood has independently confirmed a data-exfiltration event materially affecting the customer, subject to mutual cooperation and reasonable opportunity to investigate. We recommend an MSA addendum that: (a) defines severity classes, (b) identifies required cooperation steps, and (c) clarifies regulatory filing responsibilities.

- For EU regulatory filings, Redwood will provide reasonable assistance (evidence, logs, templates) and, where requested, will coordinate with customer counsel; Redwood is not the party of record for statutory filings unless explicitly agreed.

Next steps we propose:
1) Camila/GreenFinTech: confirm desired severity definitions.
2) Redwood legal: prepare draft MSA addendum (redline) and upload to DocuSign for review — target EOD Friday. Link: https://docusign.com/packet/ABC-IR-POC-DRAFT
3) Claire: if auditor needs tabletop exercise artifacts, please list specific artifacts (dates, control IDs) and we'll pull redacted test logs.

I'll attach an initial redline and reference SOC2 excerpt to the DocuSign packet.

Regards,
